title: Runtime experiment lab protocols and kernel fuzz suite 2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This page documents the Runtime Experiment Lab protocols and the Kernel Fuzz Suite (KFS): a repeatable, auditable set of experiments and tooling we use to exercise scheduling, kernel selection, and execution edge cases in the Redwood serving runtime. The goal is to find latent correctness bugs and fidelity regressions, validate mitigation strategies, and produce reproducible artifacts for profiling and remediation teams.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all internal runtime kernel builds and scheduler releases before a canary rollout.
- Targets GPU and accelerator execution layers, batch slicing, KV-cache prefetch pathways, and scheduler handoff code paths.
- Not intended for customer-facing load testing or production-scale benchmarking (see the benchmarking catalog).

Owning team and contacts
-----------------------
- Primary owner: Eng - Serving Runtime (runtime-experiments@redwood.example.com)
- Experiment custodian (lab ops): Aisha Patel
- Observability liaison: Marco Nguyen
- Security reviewer: Lin Chen
- Slack channel: #runtime-lab

Motivation and success criteria
-------------------------------
Why we run a fuzzing/testbed program:
- Many kernel regressions are non-deterministic and appear only under complex interleavings of scheduling and batching.
- Automated fuzzing can expose correctness issues (bad memory accesses, kernel crashes), API contract regressions (inference fidelity changes), and performance cliffs.
- Success criteria for a release candidate: zero reproducible kernel crashes, fidelity drift within defined bounds, and no unexplained tail-latency increases after exercising the KFS and protocol suite.

High-level testbed architecture
-------------------------------
Components and their roles:
- Lab controller: lightweight service that orchestrates experiments, collects artifacts, and uploads to the experiment bucket (s3://redwood-runtime-lab).
- Isolated runner cluster: ephemeral fleet of instances with representative accelerator types (A100/RTX/Custom). Each runner is instrumented with the profiler agent and secure collector.
- Kernel harness: small shim that loads the runtime binary, injects test inputs, and toggles kernel-selection flags.
- Fuzzer engine: mutated input generator + workload orchestrator (see KFS modules).
- Observability stack: traces (X-Ray/Jaeger), perf kernels, GPU telemetry (SM utilization, memory histograms), aggregated into the runtime-lab dashboard.

Kernel Fuzz Suite (KFS) components
----------------------------------
- Input mutation engine (IM): generates permutations of sequence lengths, prompt/prefix shapes, and KV-cache states.
- Scheduling combinator (SC): composes concurrency shapes and priority mixes (e.g., 80% background low-priority long seq, 20% high-priority short seq bursts).
- Kernel toggler (KT): flips kernel selection heuristics and quantization code paths at runtime to test fallback logic.
- State snapshotter (SS): captures kernel inputs, memory maps, and KV cache deltas for deterministic replay.
- Crash triage agent (CTA): automatic symbolication and core extraction; posts to lab bug queue with attachments.

Representative KFS testcases (examples)
--------------------------------------
1) Mixed-fidelity handoff: 500 low-priority requests with sequence=512 interleaved with high-priority requests sequence=64 every 30ms. Kernel toggles to half-precision for background path.
2) KV-cache eviction race: two tenants share a shard; induce eviction threshold crossing while prefetcher runs.
3) Preemption + batch-slice race: synthetic workloads that induce cooperative preemption, followed by load spike to trigger slice reassembly logic.
4) Cross-kernel migration: on-the-fly switch from optimized attention kernel A to fallback kernel B with KV merge.

Experiment protocol (must be followed exactly)
--------------------------------------------
Preconditions: runner images are built from the release candidate branch, instrumentation flags enabled, and lab controller at v1.4.

1. Reserve lab quota: create a lab ticket in the tracker and tag the candidate.
2. Provision ephemeral runners using the lab controller: `labctl provision --flavor=a100-small --count=4 --tag=rc-1234`
3. Upload the release candidate binary to s3 and sign the artifact: `aws s3 cp build/runtime-rc-1234.tar.gz s3://redwood-runtime-lab/rc-1234/`
4. Start baseline sweep: run KFS quick-check suite (5m smoke) to assert no immediate crashes. `labctl run-suite --suite=kfs-quick --rc=rc-1234`
5. Run targeted fuzz campaigns (per schedule): `labctl run-fuzz --campaign=kv-eviction-race --duration=2h --seed=42`
6. After each campaign: collect traces, snapshots, and profiler outputs. `labctl collect --rc=rc-1234 --campaign=kv-eviction-race --out=rc-1234/kv-eviction-race/`
7. If CTA reports a crash, do an immediate stop of related runners and tag the issue number in the lab ticket; escalate to the on-call kernel owner.
8. Repro attempt: use the included deterministic replay harness with snapshot produced by SS.
9. Postmortem: if crash is reproducible, run the minimal failing-case isolation and attach a replay artifact to the bug.

Metrics and observability requirements
------------------------------------
Minimum telemetry captured for every experiment run (stored alongside artifacts):
- Trace ID and flame graph (string id).
- Kernel name/variant and selection signal sequence.
- Per-request latency histogram (p50/p90/p99).
- GPU metrics: SM utilization, memory usage, PCIe transfer rates.
- Host metrics: CPU steal, context-switch rate.
- Fidelity checksums: deterministic output hash for fixed prompts, and token-by-token diffs when applicable.

Suggested thresholds (failure triggers):
| Metric | Threshold | Action |
|-------|----------:|--------|
| Crash rate | > 0 reproducible crashes | Block and triage immediately |
| P99 latency regression | > 25% over baseline | Notify perf-oncall and schedule deeper profiling |
| Fidelity drift | > 0.5% token mismatch rate for control prompts | Hold rollout and open quality regression ticket |
| Memory growth | sustained >20% over 30 minutes | Investigate leak; attach allocator traces |

Repro and isolation checklist
-----------------------------
- If a crash is observed: collect CTA bundle, mark the runner-safe image, and run `labctl replay --snapshot <id> --deterministic` to attempt reproduction.
- If non-deterministic: increase chaos seed variety and run for 24 hours with varied seeds; collect top 5 distinct stack traces.
- For fidelity issues: run the fidelity harness comparing outputs across kernel variants and quantization profiles; attach a token-diff report.

Failure modes and triage playbook (summary)
-----------------------------------------
- Kernel crash on launch: check linked libraries and driver mismatch; confirm CUDA/cuDNN versions. If mismatch, mark as infra regression and revert platform driver upgrade.
- Silent output corruption: run checksum comparisons with golden inputs, then enable per-layer logging and binary search across kernel patches.
- Tail latency spike correlated to batch reassembly: inspect scheduler traces for preemption windows and slice queuing; attach timeline view.

Security and isolation constraints
--------------------------------
- All experiment artifacts live in ACL-protected S3 bucket with lab-only read/write.
- Runners must run in an isolated VPC with NAT disabled for external test runs; allow egress for observability only via lab collector.
- No customer data may be used in experiments; anonymized synthetic corpora are provided in s3://redwood-runtime-lab/corpora/

Artifacts and retention policy
----------------------------
- Crash bundles: retained for 90 days.
- Deterministic snapshots and replay artifacts: retained for 180 days.
- Aggregated telemetry and dashboards: retained per observability policy (default 365 days).

Automation and gating for release flows
-------------------------------------
- Example CI gating rule (pseudocode):
```
if (kfs_smoke.pass && no_reproducible_crashes && fidelity_ok) {
  allow_canary=true
} else {
  block_release=true
}
```
- KFS runs are executed as part of the release pipeline (post-build, pre-canary). Full campaign runs are nightly for main branch and on-demand for RCs.

Integrations and tooling snippets
--------------------------------
- Start a campaign: `labctl run-campaign --name kernel-migration-smoke --rc rc-1234 --profile heavy-preempt`
- Fetch artifacts: `aws s3 sync s3://redwood-runtime-lab/rc-1234/kernel-migration-smoke/ ./artifacts/`
- Replay with deterministic harness: `python replay_harness.py --snapshot s3://.../snapshot-id --binary runtime-rc-1234.tar.gz`

Reporting and communication
-------------------------
- On any reproducible crash: automatically create a ticket in the kernel tracker with CTA attachments and link to the lab ticket.
- Weekly lab digest: lab-ops publishes a summary of top findings to #runtime-lab and the Engineering PagerDuty stakeholders.

Runbook: immediate steps for on-call (short)
--------------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge lab ticket and check CTA bundle.
2. If crash reproduces locally, annotate with minimal repro and assign to kernel-owner.
3. If not reproducible, request longer campaign with seed sweep and attach new artifact.
4. Coordinate with observability for deeper sampling if needed.

Appendix B: Common labctl commands
----------------------------------
- `labctl provision --flavor=<flavor> --count=<n> --tag=<tag>`
- `labctl run-suite --suite=<name> --rc=<rc>`
- `labctl collect --rc=<rc> --campaign=<name> --out=<path>`
- `labctl replay --snapshot <id> --deterministic`

Related pages and next steps
---------------------------
- Link the experiment findings to the release notes for the RC and to the performance regression huntbook when appropriate.
- Next planned enhancements: integrate fuzzing signals into the kernel autotuner and add differential fuzzing between quantized and full-precision paths.
